scene:
Three zones read left to right, separated by generous space.

LEFT ZONE, from announcement to cash, top to bottom: at the top a megaphone with plain radiating lines, labelled €8M ANNOUNCED. A navy arrow runs down from it; halfway down a small ochre pile of coins and a stack of blank legal papers are peeled off to the side along a short ochre arrow, labelled DEAL COSTS −€0.4M. The main arrow ends in a teal bank vault at the bottom, labelled €7.6M RECEIVED.

MIDDLE ZONE, an ownership ladder of four boxes stacked top to bottom and joined by short downward navy lines: an office tower labelled INVESTMENT FIRM; a round pool of coins labelled FUND; a plain small building labelled HOLDING COMPANY, with a bank building to its right sending a teal arrow into it labelled LOAN; at the bottom a busy office with a few customer figures beside it, labelled OPERATING COMPANY. Beside the FUND box, a small rising line chart with an empty open hand under it, labelled VALUATION UP: NO CASH.

RIGHT ZONE, who may approve the hires, top to bottom: a document with a ribbon seal labelled BOARD PLAN: 4 HIRES; below it a row of three person figures inside a teal frame with a large ochre check mark, labelled 3 HIRES APPROVED; below that a row of five person figures with the fifth figure crossed out by a navy line, labelled 5 HIRES: NEEDS CONSENT.

All coins are plain discs with no symbols; draw no dollar, euro or other currency signs on any object. Buildings, documents, charts and people carry no words, letters or numerals of their own; people are unlabelled.

TEXT: draw exactly these labels, each once and nothing else: €8M ANNOUNCED, DEAL COSTS −€0.4M, €7.6M RECEIVED, INVESTMENT FIRM, FUND, HOLDING COMPANY, LOAN, OPERATING COMPANY, VALUATION UP: NO CASH, BOARD PLAN: 4 HIRES, 3 HIRES APPROVED, 5 HIRES: NEEDS CONSENT. Any other text is a defect.
alt: An €8 million announcement loses €0.4 million of deal costs and leaves €7.6 million received; an ownership ladder runs from investment firm to fund to holding company, which takes a loan, to the operating company, with a note that a rising valuation pays no cash; a board plan allows four hires, three are approved and a fifth would need consent.
caption: What reaches the company, which organization holds the money and debt, and who may approve spending it.
